source.title: Fast Learning of Graph Neural Networks with Guaranteed Generalizability: One-hidden-layer Case
source.authors: Shuai Zhang; Meng Wang; Si-Jia Liu; Pin-Yu Chen; Jin-Jun Xiong

record.tranche_reason: The study gives theoretical and synthetic-experiment results for one-hidden-layer graph neural networks, a new setting relative to the claim, but does not measure the training classification error named by any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports convergence guarantees and parameter-estimation results for synthetic GNNs. Its numerical results measure parameter distance or estimation success, not training classification error; no result row matches a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study establishes parameter-recovery guarantees and reports synthetic GNN estimation experiments. It does not test any listed version: classification parameter error is not training classification error; width experiments do not measure spurious-minimum frequencies or student overparameterization; tensor initialization does not test signal propagation or trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly matches the authors' conclusion: assuming a realizable one-hidden-layer GNN and sufficient samples, tensor-initialized accelerated GD converges linearly to the regression teacher parameters or a nearby classification critical point, faster than vanilla GD. Their approximately zero classification generalization-error claim should be attributed to the authors; the explicit guarantee bounds parameter distance and does not establish near-zero classification error on stochastic Bernoulli labels.
record.recipe_differences: Uses tensor initialization followed by accelerated gradient descent, under a ground-truth model assumption; numerical initialization is randomly selected within a stated distance of W* to reduce computation. Experiments use synthetic graph data, not the listed benchmarks or recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The sample complexity and successful estimation depend on feature dimension and graph degree; the paper also analyzes dependence on graph structure and reports sample-size effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter-estimation error decreases with sample count for sigmoid binary-classification GNNs and for ReLU regression GNNs with noisy measurements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated teacher-model assumptions and nearby initialization, gradient-based training can estimate one-hidden-layer GNN parameters, with accuracy depending on sample count and label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1–2 establish local linear convergence with tensor initialization and sufficient samples; Figure 4 reports fewer iterations for accelerated GD than GD from the same nearby initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum can accelerate parameter recovery in the studied one-hidden-layer GNN teacher-student problems.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 reports slower parameter convergence as hidden width increases, while Figures 5–7 examine sample requirements across feature dimensions and graph structures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width, feature dimension, and graph properties affect convergence speed or sample requirements for GNN parameter estimation.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 108, 2020
record.problems: The experiments use synthetic graph-structured data. The displayed numerical outcomes are figures without exact values in the supplied text. The binary-classification result measures parameter distance, not classification error; the theoretical guarantees assume a ground-truth model and sufficient samples.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels, and effects of model size or training recipe.
Spurious-minimum frequencies from standard initialization as teacher and student widths grow together, and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons with identity shortcuts, special deep-network initializations, or Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient preservation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and effects on learning speed or trainable depth.
Training above the initial stability limit, loss transients, curvature adaptation, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Safran and Shamir's spurious-minima finding is cited as background. Neither the nearby initialization used numerically nor the tensor-initialization guarantee tests V2 or V4. Additional estimation and acceleration results fit no listed version, so they do not require missing claim-linked rows.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model-size effects, and the listed training recipes are not measured.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student sweep or spurious-minima frequency is tested.
No depth comparison, identity-shortcut comparison, or corresponding training-error outcome is tested.
No comparison of initialization methods for learning speed or trainable depth is reported as a result bearing on the version.
No learning-rate stability-limit experiment is reported.

rows.subject: Algorithm 1 on synthetic graph-structured data (binary classification)
rows.operation_detail: Train the one-hidden-layer GNN with accelerated gradient descent and tensor initialization; report relative parameter distance from the ground-truth model.
rows.value: figure only; the text says the distance decreases as the number of samples increases
rows.uncertainty: Averaged over 100 independent trials; no error bar stated in the text.
rows.note: This measures distance to ground-truth parameters, not training classification error. The figure supplies no extractable exact values in the provided text.
rows.check: The numerical experiment uses random initialization constrained to relative distance below 0.5 from W*, rather than tensor initialization, and reuses the whole training set each iteration. The reported decrease in parameter error is supported by Section 5.3, but cannot establish any listed version.

source_check.correct: Numerical experiments use random initialization satisfying ||W(0) − W*||F / ||W*||F < 0.5 and reuse the whole training set each iteration. Figure 9 reports decreasing relative parameter distance with increasing sample count, averaged over 100 independent trials.
source_check.problem: The operation incorrectly attributes tensor initialization to the numerical experiment.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses overparameterization and spurious minima, but the study's own results concern parameter recovery using accelerated gradient descent.

tranche.reason: Parameter recovery and sample complexity in realizable one-hidden-layer GNNs do not test any listed claim version. Neither training classification error nor the specified width, depth, initialization, stability-limit, or batch-normalization effects are tested.

source_check.notes: Both numerical rows use constrained random initialization and full-training-set gradients. Figure 8 varies labeled sample count |Ω|; its prose uses N when describing convergence toward the noise level. Exact curve values are not stated.
